sla_assessment_criteria: Different Chinese words are listened to while paying attention to Correct tones.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded text|Written materials|Downloaded videos from YouTube that show tongue twisters etc

sla_notes_intro: Chinese is a tonal language, so the pitch contour of a syllable changes its meaning. In this lesson learners listen to single words and short pairs and decide which tone they heard.
sla_notes_details: Standard Mandarin (Putonghua) has four tones plus a neutral tone. Tone 1 is high and level (ˉ), tone 2 rises like a question (ˊ), tone 3 falls and then rises (ˇ) and tone 4 falls sharply (ˋ). A neutral tone is short and light and carries no mark. Teachers model initials and finals from cards (b p m f, a o e i u ü) and learners imitate them, then listen to recorded words and raise a hand or hold up a tone card (1 to 4) for the tone they hear. The tone mark is placed on the main vowel of the final: the order of priority is a, then o or e, and for iu and ui it goes on the second vowel.
sla_notes_illustrations: The syllable ma changes meaning with each tone: mā 妈 (mother), má 麻 (hemp), mǎ 马 (horse), mà 骂 (to scold), and ma 吗 (question particle, neutral tone). The teacher says mǎ and learners hold up card 3; the teacher says shū 书 (book) and learners hold up card 1.
sla_notes_daily_life: Using the wrong tone can change what you mean, for example asking for 马 (horse) instead of 妈 (mother). Careful listening helps learners follow Chinese songs, greetings and instructions from Chinese friends, tutors or business partners.
sla_exercise: Name the four tones of Mandarin and describe the shape of each.::Tone 1 is high and level, tone 2 rises, tone 3 falls then rises, and tone 4 falls sharply. There is also a light neutral tone.||Which tone does mǎ 马 (horse) carry?::It carries the third tone (falling then rising).||Give the pinyin with tone marks for 妈 (mother) and 骂 (to scold).::妈 is mā (tone 1) and 骂 is mà (tone 4).

sla_notes_intro: Learners practise saying short greetings in pairs while paying attention to the correct tone of each syllable. Accurate tones make the speaker understood the first time.
sla_notes_details: Before speaking, learners memorise each tone with a memory aid such as a hand gesture drawn in the air (flat hand for tone 1, rising hand for tone 2, dipping hand for tone 3, chopping hand for tone 4). Simple dialogues are rehearsed slowly and then at natural speed. Basic greeting patterns are 你好 nǐ hǎo (hello), 你叫什么名字? nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? (what is your name?), 我叫... wǒ jiào ... (my name is ...), 你好吗? nǐ hǎo ma? and 我很好 wǒ hěn hǎo (I am fine). Learners note that two third tones in a row change: 你好 is pronounced ní hǎo.
sla_notes_illustrations: Pair work. A: 你好! Nǐ hǎo! B: 你好! 你叫什么名字? Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? A: 我叫阿里。Wǒ jiào Ālǐ. B: 你好吗? Nǐ hǎo ma? A: 我很好,谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xièxie. Each partner checks that the tones are correct.
sla_notes_daily_life: Polite greetings in correct tones let learners talk with Chinese visitors, tourists and investors, and make a good first impression.
sla_exercise: How do you say 'hello' in Chinese, with pinyin?::你好 nǐ hǎo.||How is 你好 actually pronounced when two third tones meet?::The first third tone becomes a rising tone, so it sounds like ní hǎo.||Answer this question in Chinese: 你叫什么名字?::我叫 (your name), for example 我叫阿里 (wǒ jiào Ālǐ).

sla_notes_intro: Hanyu pinyin is the Roman-letter system used to spell the sounds of Chinese. Learners read pinyin words aloud and give every syllable its tone.
sla_notes_details: A pinyin syllable is made up of an initial (声母), a final (韵母) and a tone (声调). Examples: b + ā = bā, x + ué = xué. Some syllables have no initial, such as ā or ài. Learners read from the tone marks: mā, má, mǎ, mà. When i is written with a tone mark the dot is dropped (nǐ). Syllables are joined to make words, for example xué + xiào = xuéxiào 学校 (school) and lǎo + shī = lǎoshī 老师 (teacher). Reading is practised first with the teacher, then in chorus, then individually.
sla_notes_illustrations: Reading a word list on the board: shū (书, book), bǐ (笔, pen), lǎoshī (老师, teacher), xuésheng (学生, student), jiàoshì (教室, classroom). The learner reads each word, names the tone of every syllable and the class checks.
sla_notes_daily_life: Pinyin is the key to typing Chinese on phones and computers, looking up words in dictionaries and reading street signs and product labels in China.
sla_exercise: What three parts make up a pinyin syllable?::An initial, a final and a tone.||Read and give the tone numbers of 老师 lǎoshī.::lǎo is tone 3 and shī is tone 1.||What does 学校 xuéxiào mean?::It means school.

sla_notes_intro: Learners write Chinese words in pinyin and put each tone mark in the right place. Careful writing makes reading and later typing easier.
sla_notes_details: Tone marks are written above the main vowel of the final. Rules: if there is an a, mark the a (hǎo, bāo); if there is no a but there is o or e, mark that (gōu, měi); in iu and ui the mark goes on the last vowel (liú, huí); a single vowel takes the mark itself (nǐ, shū). Where the mark falls on i, the dot is replaced by the mark. The vowel ü is written u after j, q, x and y (jù, qù) but stays ü after n and l (nǚ, lǜ). Words are written in lower case, syllables of one word are joined, and the first letter of a name or sentence is capitalised (Tǎnsāngníyà).
sla_notes_illustrations: Dictation. The teacher says 你好, 谢谢, 老师, 学校 and learners write nǐ hǎo, xièxie, lǎoshī, xuéxiào with the correct marks. Then they swap books and mark each other's work, pointing out the position of every tone mark.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing correct pinyin helps learners text Chinese friends, type their names and label items in Chinese.
sla_exercise: On which vowel does the tone mark go in hǎo?::On the vowel a.||Write 'thank you' in pinyin with tone marks.::xièxie.||Write pinyin for the word 老师 (teacher).::lǎoshī.

sla_notes_intro: A Chinese character is built from strokes written in a fixed order and direction. Learners write characters that have between nine and eleven strokes.
sla_notes_details: Basic strokes are héng 一 (horizontal), shù 丨 (vertical), piě 丿 (left-falling), nà 丶 (right-falling or dot) and zhé 乛 (turning). Stroke order rules: top to bottom, left to right, horizontal before vertical when they cross, left-falling before right-falling, outside before inside, and close a box last. Counting strokes helps to look up characters in a dictionary. Characters are written in a square grid (田字格, tiánzìgé) so that proportions are correct. Learners trace, copy and then write from memory characters such as 是 (9 strokes), 很 (9), 高 (10), 家 (10), 校 (10), 教 (11) and 常 (11).
sla_notes_illustrations: Using a tianzige sheet, the learner writes 校 (xiào, school) in ten strokes: 木 first (four strokes) and then 交 (six strokes), left part before right part. The learner counts aloud, checks the total is ten and compares it with the model.
sla_notes_daily_life: Correct handwriting is needed to write your name and short messages in Chinese, and to read handwritten notes and signs.
sla_exercise: How many strokes does 校 have?::Ten strokes.||State the rule for the order in which a horizontal and a vertical stroke are written when they cross.::The horizontal stroke is written first, then the vertical stroke.||Give two characters with 10 strokes.::Examples are 高 (gāo, tall or high) and 家 (jiā, home).

sla_notes_intro: Vocabulary about the school environment is one of the first sets of words learners need. They write the characters, the pinyin and the English meaning.
sla_notes_details: Key words: 学校 xuéxiào (school), 老师 lǎoshī (teacher), 学生 xuésheng (student), 同学 tóngxué (classmate), 教室 jiàoshì (classroom), 书 shū (book), 笔 bǐ (pen), 本子 běnzi (exercise book), 书包 shūbāo (school bag), 桌子 zhuōzi (desk), 椅子 yǐzi (chair), 黑板 hēibǎn (blackboard), 操场 cāochǎng (playground). Learners label objects in the classroom with paper tags showing character, pinyin and picture, and copy them into a vocabulary notebook. Measure words are introduced with nouns: 一本书 yì běn shū (one book), 一支笔 yì zhī bǐ (one pen).
sla_notes_illustrations: Labelling activity. Groups walk around the classroom and stick tags on objects: 黑板 hēibǎn on the board, 桌子 zhuōzi on a desk, 门 mén on the door. Each group reads its tags aloud and writes the list in pinyin.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing school words lets learners follow classroom instructions in Chinese and introduce their school to Chinese visitors or partner-school pupils.
sla_exercise: What is 老师 in English?::Teacher.||How do you write 'desk' in Chinese and pinyin?::桌子, zhuōzi.||Give the Chinese word for 'classroom'.::教室 (jiàoshì).

sla_notes_intro: Learners use the new school words to say short, correct sentences. They start by repeating a model and then create their own.
sla_notes_details: A basic sentence pattern is Subject + Verb + Object. Useful patterns: 这是... zhè shì ... (this is ...), 那是... nà shì ... (that is ...), 我有... wǒ yǒu ... (I have ...), 他是... tā shì ... (he is ...), plus the question particle 吗 for yes/no questions and the negative 不 or 没. Learners substitute words into frames in role-play and collaborative activities, for example 这是我的书 zhè shì wǒ de shū (this is my book) and 他不是老师 tā bú shì lǎoshī (he is not a teacher). Note that 不 becomes bú before a fourth tone.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role play. Learner A holds up a pen and asks 这是什么? Zhè shì shénme? Learner B answers 这是笔。Zhè shì bǐ. A asks 你有书吗? Nǐ yǒu shū ma? and B answers 我有书。Wǒ yǒu shū.
sla_notes_daily_life: Talking about school objects in Chinese helps learners take part in exchange visits and school clubs with Chinese-speaking friends.
sla_exercise: Translate 'This is my book' into Chinese.::这是我的书 (zhè shì wǒ de shū).||What does 你有书吗? mean?::It means 'Do you have a book?'||Why is 不是 pronounced bú shì?::Because 不 changes from bù to bú before a fourth-tone syllable.

sla_notes_intro: Learners write short, complete sentences using school vocabulary, with characters and pinyin, and end each with proper punctuation.
sla_notes_details: A written sentence starts with the subject and ends with a full stop 。 Chinese punctuation takes a full-width form: 。 (full stop), ， (comma), ？ (question mark) and ！ (exclamation mark), and each occupies one character space. Learners build sentences from word cards, then copy and write them in the tianzige exercise book. Simple sentences: 我是学生 wǒ shì xuésheng (I am a student), 这是教室 zhè shì jiàoshì (this is the classroom), 老师有书 lǎoshī yǒu shū (the teacher has a book). Games such as word searches and crosswords consolidate spelling.
sla_notes_illustrations: The teacher gives the words 我, 的, 老师, 是, 数学 and learners arrange them to form 我的老师是数学老师。Wǒ de lǎoshī shì shùxué lǎoshī. (My teacher is a mathematics teacher.) They write it in characters and pinyin.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing simple sentences lets learners write name tags, notes to classmates and short messages in Chinese.
sla_exercise: Write 'I am a student' in Chinese and pinyin.::我是学生。Wǒ shì xuésheng.||Which punctuation mark ends a question in Chinese?::The question mark ？||Arrange to form a sentence: 教室 / 这 / 是::这是教室。Zhè shì jiàoshì.

learning_activity_name: Use directional noun such as in front of, and behind to express locations
sla_assessment_criteria: Locations are expressed by using directional nouns such as in front of and behind.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Directional nouns such as front and behind tell where a person or thing is. Learners use them with the verb 在 (to be at).
sla_notes_details: Common directional words: 上边 shàngbian (above), 下边 xiàbian (below), 前边 qiánbian (in front of), 后边 hòubian (behind), 左边 zuǒbian (left), 右边 yòubian (right), 里边 lǐbian (inside), 外边 wàibian (outside), 旁边 pángbiān (beside). Pattern: Thing + 在 + Place + Direction word, e.g. 书在桌子上边 shū zài zhuōzi shàngbian (the book is on the desk). Asking: ...在哪儿? ... zài nǎr? (where is ...?). Pairs practise placing objects and describing them.
sla_notes_illustrations: The teacher places a pen in front of a bag. Question: 笔在哪儿? Bǐ zài nǎr? Answer: 笔在书包前边。Bǐ zài shūbāo qiánbian. (The pen is in front of the bag.) Moving the pen behind the bag changes the answer to 后边.
sla_notes_daily_life: Directions help learners say where things are at home and school and follow simple directions from Chinese speakers.
sla_exercise: Translate 'behind' and 'in front of' into Chinese.::后边 (hòubian) and 前边 (qiánbian).||Say in Chinese: The book is on the desk.::书在桌子上边。Shū zài zhuōzi shàngbian.||What does 老师在哪儿? ask?::It asks 'Where is the teacher?'

learning_activity_name: Use conjunctions such as and, and but to construct simple oral sentences
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple oral sentences are constructed by using conjunctions such as and, and but.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Conjunctions link words and clauses. Learners use 和 and 但是 to build simple spoken sentences.
sla_notes_details: 和 hé (and) joins nouns or pronouns, not whole clauses: 我和你 wǒ hé nǐ (you and I), 苹果和香蕉 píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo (apples and bananas). 但是 dànshì or 可是 kěshì (but) joins two clauses with a contrast: 我喜欢茶,但是他喜欢咖啡 wǒ xǐhuan chá, dànshì tā xǐhuan kāfēi (I like tea but he likes coffee). In role play, learners give two opposite preferences and link them. The other conjunctions 因为 yīnwèi (because) and 所以 suǒyǐ (so) are previewed with easy examples.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role play about food. A: 你喜欢米饭吗? B: 我喜欢米饭,但是我不喜欢鱼。Wǒ xǐhuan mǐfàn, dànshì wǒ bù xǐhuan yú. (I like rice, but I do not like fish.)
sla_notes_daily_life: Linking ideas lets learners describe what they like, compare things and speak more naturally.
sla_exercise: Translate 'You and I' into Chinese.::你和我 (nǐ hé wǒ) or 我和你 (wǒ hé nǐ).||What does 但是 mean?::It means 'but'.||Complete: 我喜欢书,___ 我不喜欢笔。::但是 (dànshì).

learning_activity_name: Write simple sentences using conjunctions such as and, and but
sla_method: Real-life examples and Writing Practice Sheets
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences using conjunction such as and, and but are written.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write simple sentences that use the conjunctions 和 and 但是 with correct characters and punctuation.
sla_notes_details: In writing, a comma ， is put before 但是: 我有书，但是没有笔。 (I have a book but I have no pen.) The word 和 does not take a comma. Learners note that the negative of 有 is 没有 méiyǒu. Steps: choose two ideas, decide if they agree (use 和) or contrast (use 但是), write the sentence, add punctuation and check the characters against the vocabulary list. Real-life examples from learners' own bags and desks make the sentences meaningful.
sla_notes_illustrations: The learner writes: 我的书包里有书和笔。Wǒ de shūbāo lǐ yǒu shū hé bǐ. (In my bag there are books and pens.) 我有笔，但是没有本子。Wǒ yǒu bǐ, dànshì méiyǒu běnzi. (I have a pen but no exercise book.)
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing linked sentences prepares learners for writing simple notes and messages to Chinese-speaking friends.
sla_exercise: Write in Chinese: I have a book and a pen.::我有书和笔。Wǒ yǒu shū hé bǐ.||Where does the comma go in 我有书但是没有笔?::Before 但是: 我有书，但是没有笔。||How do you say 'do not have' in Chinese?::没有 (méiyǒu).

learning_activity_name: Practice pronunciation of words from oral and audio/visual sources
sla_method: Repeat what you hear and Listen for tone and intonation
sla_assessment_criteria: Pronunciation of words from oral and audio/visual sources is practised.
sla_teaching_aids: Downloaded video or audio related to learning contents|ICT tools
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to Chinese words on audio or video and repeat them, working on initials, finals and tones.
sla_notes_details: Method: the teacher plays a word, learners repeat in chorus, then in groups, then individually. Attention is paid to difficult sounds for Swahili and English speakers: the aspirated and unaspirated pairs b/p, d/t, g/k, the retroflex zh, ch, sh, r, and the palatals j, q, x. Note that in pinyin j sounds like a soft 'j', q like 'ch' with a puff of air, and x like 'sh' made with the tongue tip lowered. Learners listen for tone and intonation of the speaker and mark the tone on word lists.
sla_notes_illustrations: Minimal pairs. The audio says bā 八 (eight) and pā 趴 (to lie prone); jī 鸡 (chicken) and qī 七 (seven); xī 西 (west) and shī 诗 (poem). Learners repeat each pair and say which one they heard.
sla_notes_daily_life: Clear pronunciation makes learners easy to understand when they speak with Chinese people or use voice assistants and translation apps.
sla_exercise: Name two pairs of sounds that differ by aspiration.::For example b and p, d and t, or g and k.||How is 七 pronounced in pinyin?::qī (tone 1).||Why do learners listen to recordings more than once?::To hear the tone and pronunciation clearly and to imitate them accurately.

sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to short classroom instructions in Chinese and respond by doing the action.
sla_notes_details: Common classroom instructions: 请坐 qǐng zuò (please sit), 请站起来 qǐng zhàn qǐlai (please stand up), 请安静 qǐng ānjìng (please be quiet), 请听 qǐng tīng (please listen), 请看黑板 qǐng kàn hēibǎn (please look at the board), 请打开书 qǐng dǎkāi shū (please open your book), 请读 qǐng dú (please read), 举手 jǔ shǒu (raise your hand), 请再说一遍 qǐng zài shuō yí biàn (please say it again). The word 请 qǐng makes a polite request. A field-trip activity (for example a visit to the school canteen) is used to practise instructions in a real setting.
sla_notes_illustrations: Total physical response. The teacher says 请站起来 and learners stand; 请坐 and they sit; 请打开书 and they open their books; 请看黑板 and they look at the board.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding simple instructions helps learners follow directions at Chinese-language centres, in shops and when working with Chinese partners.
sla_exercise: What does 请坐 mean?::Please sit down.||Give the Chinese for 'Please open your book'.::请打开书 (qǐng dǎkāi shū).||What does the word 请 add to an instruction?::It makes the request polite (please).

learning_activity_name: Listen and reproduce simple sentences
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences are listened and produced.

sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to short Chinese sentences and repeat them accurately, keeping tone and rhythm.
sla_notes_details: Active listening steps: listen to the whole sentence, listen again and notice key words, repeat in chunks (my name / is / Ali), then repeat the whole sentence. Sentences should be short and about known topics, for example 我是学生 wǒ shì xuésheng, 我们是同学 wǒmen shì tóngxué, 她是我的老师 tā shì wǒ de lǎoshī. Rhythm groups are marked with slashes and stress falls on the last important word. Gallery work is used: sentences are placed on the walls and learners listen to audio at each station and repeat.
sla_notes_illustrations: Audio: 我们是同学。Wǒmen shì tóngxué. (We are classmates.) The learner listens, repeats slowly wǒ-men / shì / tóng-xué and then at normal speed, and the teacher corrects tone 2 on tóng.
sla_notes_daily_life: Being able to repeat what you hear is the first step towards conversation, singing Chinese songs and learning new words from native speakers.
sla_exercise: How do you say 'We are classmates' in Chinese?::我们是同学 (wǒmen shì tóngxué).||What is the pronoun 她 (tā) in English?::She.||Why are long sentences repeated in chunks?::Chunking makes it easier to remember words and keep the tones right.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to read and understand various texts
learning_activity_name: Read and respond to instructions presented in a simple text
sla_name: Reading and responding to written instructions
sla_assessment_criteria: Instructions presented in a simple text are read and responded.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read short written instructions in a simple text and respond to them correctly.
sla_notes_details: Written instructions contain verbs of command such as 请写 qǐng xiě (please write), 请读 qǐng dú (please read), 请回答 qǐng huídá (please answer), 请看图 qǐng kàn tú (look at the picture), 请连线 qǐng liánxiàn (match). Reading strategy: find the verb, find the object, and do the action. Learners underline the verb and the object, translate the instruction in their own words and carry it out. Comprehension exercises use short worksheets with pinyin above the characters.
sla_notes_illustrations: Worksheet line: 请写你的名字。Qǐng xiě nǐ de míngzi. (Please write your name.) The learner underlines 写 (write) and 名字 (name) and writes their name. Next line: 请读句子。Qǐng dú jùzi. (Please read the sentence.)
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading instructions is needed for using exam papers, textbooks, apps and labels written in Chinese.
sla_exercise: What does 请写你的名字 ask you to do?::Please write your name.||What is 请读 in English?::Please read.||Which word in 请回答 means 'answer'?::回答 (huídá).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to read and understand various texts
learning_activity_name: Read a simple text and answer questions based on it
sla_name: Reading a simple text and answering questions
sla_method: Pre - reading strategies and Active reading
sla_assessment_criteria: Questions based on simple text are read and answered.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read a short text in Chinese and answer questions on its content.
sla_notes_details: Pre-reading: look at the title and pictures and predict. While reading: scan the headings, find the key words and read the text twice. Post-reading: answer who, what, where questions using question words 谁 shéi (who), 什么 shénme (what), 哪儿 nǎr (where), 几 jǐ (how many), 吗 ma (yes/no). Answers are given in full sentences to practise word order. Active reading also involves underlining new words and adding them to the vocabulary book.
sla_notes_illustrations: Text: 我叫玛丽。我是学生。我的学校很大。Wǒ jiào Mǎlì. Wǒ shì xuésheng. Wǒ de xuéxiào hěn dà. (My name is Mary. I am a student. My school is big.) Q: 玛丽是老师吗? A: 玛丽不是老师,她是学生。
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading and answering questions is the basis for comprehension in exams and for understanding notices, news and messages.
sla_exercise: What is the question word for 'what' in Chinese?::什么 (shénme).||Answer: 玛丽是学生吗? (Mary is a student, isn't she?)::是,玛丽是学生。(Yes, Mary is a student.)||What does 我的学校很大 mean?::My school is big.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Show the right response in various communicative contexts
learning_activity_name: Listen and respond to complex orders given in a school setting
sla_name: Responding to complex spoken orders in school
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex orders given in a school setting are listened and responded.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to longer orders with two or more steps in a school setting and carry them out in order.
sla_notes_details: Complex orders combine actions with sequence words: 先...然后... xiān ... ránhòu ... (first ... then ...), and location words. Example: 请先打开书,然后读第五页 (please first open your book, then read page five). Learners practise with numbers 一 to 一百 and page or line numbers, for instance 第五页 dì wǔ yè (page five). Practice exercises use recorded orders and the teacher's live orders. Learners repeat the order to confirm before acting: 好的,我先... hǎo de, wǒ xiān ...
sla_notes_illustrations: Order: 请你先把书放在桌子上,然后去黑板前边。Qǐng nǐ xiān bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shàng, ránhòu qù hēibǎn qiánbian. The learner puts the book on the desk and then goes to the front of the board.
sla_notes_daily_life: Following multi-step orders is useful in school, laboratories, workplaces and when someone gives directions.
sla_exercise: What does 先...然后... express?::It expresses the order of actions: first ... then ...||Translate: 请先读,然后写。::Please read first, and then write.||How do you say 'page five' in Chinese?::第五页 (dì wǔ yè).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Show the right response in various communicative contexts
learning_activity_name: Participate in simple discussions on topics associated with the school environment
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple discussions on topics associated with the school environment are participated in.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners join a simple discussion in Chinese on familiar school topics such as subjects, teachers and timetable.
sla_notes_details: Useful expressions: 你喜欢什么课? nǐ xǐhuan shénme kè? (what subject do you like?), 我喜欢数学 wǒ xǐhuan shùxué, 因为... yīnwèi ... (because ...), 我觉得... wǒ juéde ... (I think ...), 同意 tóngyì (agree), 不同意 bù tóngyì (disagree). Subject words: 汉语 Hànyǔ, 英语 Yīngyǔ, 数学 shùxué, 科学 kēxué, 历史 lìshǐ, 地理 dìlǐ. In group discussion each learner takes a turn, listens to others and adds one sentence. A news story about the school can serve as the topic.
sla_notes_illustrations: Group of four. A: 你喜欢什么课? B: 我喜欢汉语。汉语很有意思。Wǒ xǐhuan Hànyǔ. Hànyǔ hěn yǒu yìsi. (Chinese is interesting.) C: 我喜欢数学。
sla_notes_daily_life: Discussion skills help learners share opinions in school clubs and debate and communicate with Chinese exchange students.
sla_exercise: Say 'I like mathematics' in Chinese.::我喜欢数学 (wǒ xǐhuan shùxué).||What does 同意 mean?::Agree.||Translate 你喜欢什么课?::What subject do you like?

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Show the right response in various communicative contexts
learning_activity_name: Read and respond to complex orders given in a school setting
sla_name: Reading and responding to written orders in school
sla_method: Active Listening and Clarification of orders
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex orders given in a school setting are read and responded.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read written orders of some length in the school setting and respond by acting or writing an answer.
sla_notes_details: Written orders may appear on notice boards, worksheets or in class chat. Example verbs: 交 jiāo (hand in), 带 dài (bring), 准备 zhǔnbèi (prepare), 完成 wánchéng (finish), 检查 jiǎnchá (check). Steps: read the whole order, underline the verbs and the time or place words, clarify anything unclear by asking 请问,这是什么意思? qǐngwèn, zhè shì shénme yìsi? (excuse me, what does this mean?), and carry it out. Learners then reply in writing: 好的,我明天带书 hǎo de, wǒ míngtiān dài shū.
sla_notes_illustrations: Notice: 明天请带汉语书和本子。Míngtiān qǐng dài Hànyǔ shū hé běnzi. (Tomorrow please bring your Chinese book and exercise book.) Reply: 好的,老师。Hǎo de, lǎoshī.
sla_notes_daily_life: This skill helps learners understand school notices, homework instructions and group chat messages.
sla_exercise: What does 带 mean?::To bring or carry.||Translate 明天 into English.::Tomorrow.||How do you ask 'What does this mean?' politely?::请问,这是什么意思? (qǐngwèn, zhè shì shénme yìsi?)

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to read correctly various texts
learning_activity_name: Read different words with the required speed, correct tone and pronunciation
sla_name: Reading words aloud with speed and correct tone
sla_method: Reading aloud and Read for Comprehension
sla_assessment_criteria: Different words are read with the required speed, correct tone and pronunciation.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read Chinese words aloud at a natural pace, pronouncing every syllable and tone accurately.
sla_notes_details: Reading aloud develops fluency. Steps: teacher models, class reads together, small groups read, then individuals read. Speed increases gradually: start slowly to get the tones right, then increase to a natural rate without dropping tones. Comprehension exercises after reading confirm meaning. Learners record themselves and compare with a model. Word lists include two-syllable words such as 学习 xuéxí (study), 朋友 péngyou (friend), 老师 lǎoshī, 谢谢 xièxie and 再见 zàijiàn.
sla_notes_illustrations: Word-list reading. The learner reads 学习 xuéxí, 朋友 péngyou, 老师 lǎoshī, 谢谢 xièxie, 再见 zàijiàn at a steady speed. The teacher notes that 朋友 ends in a neutral tone and 谢谢 has a neutral second syllable.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading aloud clearly is important for presentations, reciting poems and reading announcements in Chinese.
sla_exercise: Name two skills practised in reading aloud.::Correct pronunciation and tones, and fluent reading speed.||Which syllable in 朋友 péngyou has the neutral tone?::The second syllable 友.||How do you say 'goodbye' in Chinese?::再见 (zàijiàn).

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in a variety of contexts
specific_competence_name: Develop an understanding of the characteristics of spoken and written language
learning_activity_name: Use appropriately the four tones, the neutral/zero tone and their changes in oral communication
sla_name: Using the four tones and the neutral tone in speech
sla_assessment_criteria: The four tones, the neutral/zero tone and their changes are used appropriately in oral communication.
sla_teaching_aids: Videos|Games on how to use tones|Pictures that display tones
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners learn how tones change in connected speech and how the neutral tone is used in everyday words.
sla_notes_details: Rules of tone change: (1) two third tones together: the first becomes second (你好 nǐ hǎo is said ní hǎo). (2) 不 bù becomes bú before a fourth tone (不是 bú shì, 不去 bú qù). (3) 一 yī becomes yí before a fourth tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before tones 1, 2 and 3 (一天 yì tiān, 一年 yì nián, 一起 yì qǐ). The neutral tone is short and light in words such as 妈妈 māma, 爸爸 bàba, 谢谢 xièxie, 朋友 péngyou, and in particles 的, 了, 吗, 吧. The pitch of a neutral syllable depends on the tone before it (it is relatively high after tone 3 and lowest after tone 4). Role-playing dialogues embed these changes.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue with tone change: A: 你去学校吗? Nǐ qù xuéxiào ma? B: 不去,我在家。Bú qù, wǒ zài jiā. (No, I am at home.) 不 changes to bú before qù (4th tone).
sla_notes_daily_life: Correct tone changes make speech sound natural, which helps learners talk with Chinese speakers and understand them in real time.
sla_exercise: How is 不是 pronounced?::bú shì; 不 changes to the second tone before a fourth tone.||Give two words that have a neutral tone.::For example 妈妈 māma and 谢谢 xièxie.||How is 一个 pronounced?::yí gè.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in a variety of contexts
specific_competence_name: Develop an understanding of the characteristics of spoken and written language
learning_activity_name: Use punctuation marks correctly in writing simple texts (full stop, comma, apostrophe, question mark, exclamation mark etc)
sla_name: Using punctuation marks correctly in writing
sla_assessment_criteria: Punctuation marks are used correctly in writing simple texts (full stop, comma, apostrophe, question mark, exclamation mark etc.).
sla_teaching_aids: Videos|Games on how to use tones|Pictures that display tones
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners use Chinese punctuation marks correctly when they write simple texts.
sla_notes_details: Chinese punctuation is written in full-width form and takes its own space. 。 (句号 jùhào, full stop) ends a statement. ， (逗号 dòuhào, comma) separates parts of a sentence. 、 (顿号 dùnhào, enumeration comma) separates items in a list: 苹果、香蕉、芒果. ？ (问号 wènhào) ends a question. ！ (感叹号 gǎntànhào) marks exclamation or command. In vertical layout marks appear at the lower right, in horizontal writing at the lower left of the character. Learners use prompts such as pictures to write short texts and then check every mark.
sla_notes_illustrations: Text with marks: 我有苹果、香蕉和芒果。你呢? Wǒ yǒu píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo hé mángguǒ. Nǐ ne? (I have apples, bananas and mangoes. And you?) The learner identifies 、 in the list, 。 at the end of the first sentence and ？ after 你呢.
sla_notes_daily_life: Punctuation helps make written messages clear and avoids misunderstanding in text messages, letters and homework.
sla_exercise: Which Chinese mark separates items in a list?::The enumeration comma 、 (dùnhào).||What is the Chinese name for the full stop?::句号 (jùhào).||Punctuate: 你叫什么名字::你叫什么名字?

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in a variety of contexts
specific_competence_name: Developing the ability to communicate orally
learning_activity_name: Participate in simple conversation (e.g. greetings)
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple conversation is participated in (e.g. greetings).
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners take part in simple greeting conversations, using correct tones, polite forms and simple questions and answers.
sla_notes_details: Greetings by time of day: 早上好 zǎoshang hǎo (good morning), 下午好 xiàwǔ hǎo (good afternoon), 晚上好 wǎnshang hǎo (good evening), 晚安 wǎn'ān (good night). Introductions: 我叫... wǒ jiào ..., 我是... wǒ shì ..., 我是坦桑尼亚人 wǒ shì Tǎnsāngníyà rén (I am Tanzanian), 认识你很高兴 rènshi nǐ hěn gāoxìng (nice to meet you). Farewells: 再见 zàijiàn, 明天见 míngtiān jiàn (see you tomorrow). Politeness: 请 qǐng, 谢谢 xièxie, 不客气 bú kèqi (you are welcome), 对不起 duìbuqǐ (sorry), 没关系 méi guānxi (never mind). Think-pair-share is used: think, discuss with a partner and share with the class.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue. A: 早上好! Zǎoshang hǎo! B: 早上好! 你叫什么名字? A: 我叫萨米。认识你很高兴。Wǒ jiào Sāmǐ. Rènshi nǐ hěn gāoxìng. B: 认识你我也很高兴。再见! A: 再见!
sla_notes_daily_life: Greeting in Chinese is a friendly way to start relationships with visitors, business people and friends from China.
sla_exercise: Say 'Good morning' in Chinese.::早上好 (zǎoshang hǎo).||What is the reply to 谢谢?::不客气 (bú kèqi), meaning 'you are welcome'.||Translate 认识你很高兴.::Nice to meet you.

specific_competence_name: Develop awareness of Chinese phonemes, initial, final, tone and characters
learning_activity_name: Listen to different Chinese words and mark tones on their positions
sla_assessment_criteria: Different Chinese words and tones are marked-on their positions.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded text|Written materials|Downloaded videos from YouTube that show tongue twisters etc
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to Chinese words and mark the tone on the correct vowel. This links what they hear to what they write.
sla_notes_details: Rules for tone position: the mark goes on a if it is present (hǎo, māo); otherwise on o or e (zhōu, dōu, xiě); in iu and ui it goes on the second vowel (jiǔ, duì); and on i or u when it stands alone (nǐ, shū). When i carries a tone the dot is replaced by the mark. Learners listen to a word, write the toneless pinyin, and then add the mark. Colour is used to distinguish tones (red for tone 1, blue for tone 2, green for tone 3, black for tone 4). Words are chosen from home and daily life: māma, bàba, gēge, jiějie, dìdi, mèimei.
sla_notes_illustrations: Listening task. The teacher says 爸爸, 哥哥, 姐姐, 弟弟 and learners write bàba, gēge, jiějie, dìdi with tone marks on the right vowels, e.g. jiějie has a third tone on the e of the first syllable and a neutral tone on the second.
sla_notes_daily_life: Marking tones correctly helps learners spell names and words in Chinese chat, dictionaries and language apps.
sla_exercise: On which vowel does the tone mark go in 学 xué?::On the e, giving xué.||Where does the mark go in jiǔ (九, nine)?::On the last vowel, u.||Add the tone: 爸爸 (father), ba ba, first syllable fourth tone.::bàba.

specific_competence_name: Develop awareness of Chinese phonemes, initial, final, tone and characters
learning_activity_name: Write the Chinese words while observing tone positions
sla_name: Writing words with correct tone positions
sla_assessment_criteria: Chinese words are written while observing tone positions.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded text|Written materials|Downloaded videos from YouTube that show tongue twisters etc
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write Chinese words in pinyin and place the tone mark correctly on each syllable.
sla_notes_details: Learners apply the rules to their written work: mark the a first, then o or e, and the second vowel of iu and ui. When writing a word of several syllables, each syllable is marked separately and neutral-tone syllables get no mark (māma). Names of people and places begin with a capital letter and the syllables are joined: Dálèisīsàlāmǔ for Dar es Salaam, Tǎnsāngníyà for Tanzania. Mnemonic aids such as 'a first, o and e next, then the last of iu/ui' help learners remember the rules and digital tools such as a pinyin keyboard help them practise.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dictation of family words: the teacher says 爷爷 奶奶 妈妈 and the learner writes yéye, nǎinai, māma. The partner checks that the mark on nǎinai is on the a and that the second syllable is neutral.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing tones correctly is needed to type Chinese with a pinyin keyboard and to spell names and addresses correctly.
sla_exercise: Write the pinyin of 奶奶 (grandmother).::nǎinai.||What is the rule for placing a tone mark on a syllable containing a?::The mark is written on the a.||Where is the tone mark in duì 对?::On the i, the second vowel of ui.

specific_competence_name: Develop awareness of Chinese phonemes, initial, final, tone and characters
learning_activity_name: Write Chinese characters with 12-13 strokes
sla_name: Writing Chinese characters of 12 to 13 strokes
sla_assessment_criteria: Chinese characters with 12-13 strokes are written.
sla_teaching_aids: Recorded text|Written materials|Downloaded videos from YouTube that show tongue twisters etc
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write characters of twelve and thirteen strokes carefully, following the stroke order rules.
sla_notes_details: Characters with 12 strokes include 就 jiù (then), 喝 hē (drink), 湖 hú (lake) and 等 děng (wait). Characters with 13 strokes include 想 xiǎng (think, want), 新 xīn (new), 睡 shuì (sleep) and 楼 lóu (building). Components are written in order: left to right, top to bottom. For 想, the top part 相 is written first (木 then 目) and 心 (heart) is written last. Learners break a character into radicals: 喝 = 口 (mouth) + 曷; 睡 = 目 (eye) + 垂. Mnemonics and digital tools such as stroke-order animation apps help.
sla_notes_illustrations: The learner writes 想 (xiǎng) in the tianzige: 木 (4 strokes), 目 (5 strokes), 心 (4 strokes), total 13. The learner counts strokes aloud and checks the balance of the character.
sla_notes_daily_life: Correct characters are essential for writing personal letters, greeting cards and social media messages in Chinese.
sla_exercise: How many strokes does 想 have?::Thirteen strokes.||Give two characters that have 12 strokes.::For example 就 (jiù) and 喝 (hē).||What radical (component) means 'mouth' in 喝?::口.

specific_competence_name: Master the correct Chinese vocabulary in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Write new words associated with the home environment
sla_assessment_criteria: New words associated with the home environment are written.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The home is a familiar topic. Learners write words for family members, rooms and household objects.
sla_notes_details: Family: 爸爸 bàba, 妈妈 māma, 哥哥 gēge (elder brother), 姐姐 jiějie (elder sister), 弟弟 dìdi (younger brother), 妹妹 mèimei (younger sister), 爷爷 yéye, 奶奶 nǎinai. Rooms: 客厅 kètīng (living room), 厨房 chúfáng (kitchen), 卧室 wòshì (bedroom), 厕所 cèsuǒ (toilet). Objects: 床 chuáng (bed), 桌子 zhuōzi (table), 椅子 yǐzi (chair), 电视 diànshì (television), 门 mén (door), 窗户 chuānghu (window). Learners label the rooms of a house drawing in characters and pinyin, and use the measure word 个 gè and 间 jiān (rooms).
sla_notes_illustrations: Picture labelling. Learners draw a house and write 厨房 chúfáng near the cooking area, 卧室 wòshì by the bed and 客厅 kètīng by the sofa, then list the family members who use each room.
sla_notes_daily_life: The vocabulary allows learners to describe their family and home to Chinese-speaking friends and to understand the language of household products.
sla_exercise: Write 'kitchen' in Chinese and pinyin.::厨房, chúfáng.||What is 弟弟 in English?::Younger brother.||Which word means 'bedroom'?::卧室 (wòshì).

specific_competence_name: Master the correct Chinese vocabulary in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Construct simple oral sentences using new words associated with the home environment
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple oral sentences using new words associated with the home environment are Constructed.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners build spoken sentences using home vocabulary, describing people, rooms and objects.
sla_notes_details: Sentence patterns: 我家有... wǒ jiā yǒu ... (my family has ...), 我家有五口人 wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén (there are five people in my family), 这是我的妈妈 zhè shì wǒ de māma (this is my mother), 厨房很大 chúfáng hěn dà (the kitchen is big). Adjectives take 很 as a link, not 是: 房子很大, not 房子是大. Questions: 你家有几口人? nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén? Learners use role-playing to introduce their families and collaborate to describe a picture.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role play. A: 你家有几口人? Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén? B: 我家有六口人:爸爸、妈妈、哥哥、妹妹、弟弟和我。Wǒ jiā yǒu liù kǒu rén: bàba, māma, gēge, mèimei, dìdi hé wǒ.
sla_notes_daily_life: Talking about the family is the first topic in most conversations with new Chinese-speaking friends.
sla_exercise: How do you ask 'How many people are in your family?'::你家有几口人? (nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?)||Translate: 我的厨房很大。::My kitchen is big.||Why do we say 房子很大 and not 房子是大?::Adjective predicates use 很 (or another adverb) and not 是.

specific_competence_name: Master the correct Chinese vocabulary in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Write simple sentences using new words associated with the home environment
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences using new words associated with the home environment are written.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write simple sentences about the home, using correct characters, word order and punctuation.
sla_notes_details: Word order in Chinese sentences is Subject + Time + Place + Verb + Object. Examples: 我家在坦桑尼亚 wǒ jiā zài Tǎnsāngníyà (my home is in Tanzania), 我爸爸在厨房 wǒ bàba zài chúfáng (my father is in the kitchen). Learners write sentences from picture prompts, use the enumeration comma 、 for lists of family members and end with 。 They are encouraged to use interactive games (word searches, crosswords) to fix spelling, and to read their sentences aloud after writing.
sla_notes_illustrations: Picture prompt: a kitchen with a mother cooking. Sentence: 妈妈在厨房做饭。Māma zài chúfáng zuò fàn. (Mother is cooking in the kitchen.)
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing about home prepares learners to write short self-introductions, messages and emails to Chinese friends.
sla_exercise: Write in Chinese: My father is in the sitting room.::我爸爸在客厅。Wǒ bàba zài kètīng.||What is the correct word order of a Chinese sentence?::Subject, time, place, verb, object.||Translate 妈妈在厨房。::Mother is in the kitchen.

specific_competence_name: Develop the use of appropriate grammar and vocabulary in conversation and writing
learning_activity_name: Use appropriate preposition such as at, on, in, to express locations
sla_assessment_criteria: Locations are expressed using appropriate prepositions such as at, on, in and to.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Prepositions such as 在, 从 and 到 show place and direction. Learners use them in short sentences about where things are and where people go.
sla_notes_details: 在 zài (at, in, on) shows position: 我在学校 wǒ zài xuéxiào (I am at school). 从 cóng (from) shows origin: 我从坦桑尼亚来 wǒ cóng Tǎnsāngníyà lái (I come from Tanzania). 到 dào (to, arrive at) shows a destination: 我到学校 wǒ dào xuéxiào. 去 qù (go) and 来 lái (come) are verbs of motion. 给 gěi (to, for) marks the receiver. Prepositional phrases come before the verb: 我在家学习 wǒ zài jiā xuéxí (I study at home). A map of Tanzania is used to practise regions and towns: 从达累斯萨拉姆到多多马 cóng Dálèisīsàlāmǔ dào Duōduōmǎ (from Dar es Salaam to Dodoma).
sla_notes_illustrations: Map task. Learners say 我从阿鲁沙到姆万扎 wǒ cóng Ālǔshā dào Mǔwànzhā (I am going from Arusha to Mwanza) and 我在莫希 wǒ zài Mòxī (I am in Moshi), then write two similar sentences.
sla_notes_daily_life: Prepositions of place are needed for giving addresses, saying where you come from and describing journeys.
sla_exercise: Translate 'I come from Tanzania'.::我从坦桑尼亚来 (wǒ cóng Tǎnsāngníyà lái).||What is the meaning of 在 in 我在家?::At (I am at home).||Where does the phrase 在家 go in the sentence 我在家学习?::Before the verb 学习.

specific_competence_name: Develop the use of appropriate grammar and vocabulary in conversation and writing
learning_activity_name: Participate in conversations about telling time
sla_assessment_criteria: Conversations about time telling are participated in.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners ask for and give the time in Chinese and take part in short dialogues about daily schedules.
sla_notes_details: Question: 现在几点? xiànzài jǐ diǎn? (what time is it now?). Answers: 现在三点 (three o'clock), 三点五分 sān diǎn wǔ fēn (3:05), 三点一刻 sān diǎn yí kè (3:15), 三点半 sān diǎn bàn (3:30), 差五分四点 chà wǔ fēn sì diǎn (five minutes to four), 两点 liǎng diǎn (2 o'clock, note liǎng not èr). Time words come before the verb: 我七点起床 wǒ qī diǎn qǐchuáng (I get up at seven). Days: 星期一 xīngqī yī (Monday) to 星期日 xīngqī rì (Sunday). Map searching and pair practice make the conversations real.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue. A: 现在几点? Xiànzài jǐ diǎn? B: 现在七点半。Xiànzài qī diǎn bàn. A: 你几点上课? Nǐ jǐ diǎn shàng kè? B: 我八点上课。Wǒ bā diǎn shàng kè.
sla_notes_daily_life: Telling time helps learners arrange meetings, follow timetables and make appointments in Chinese.
sla_exercise: How do you say '3:30' in Chinese?::三点半 (sān diǎn bàn).||Why do we say 两点 and not 二点 for 2 o'clock?::Because 两 liǎng is used with measure words and time units instead of 二 èr.||Ask 'What time is it now?' in Chinese.::现在几点? (xiànzài jǐ diǎn?)

specific_competence_name: Develop the use of appropriate grammar and vocabulary in conversation and writing
learning_activity_name: Write simple sentences about telling time
sla_method: Songs and rhymes and Real-life examples
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences about time telling are written.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write short sentences about their daily routine and the time of activities.
sla_notes_details: Time words come after the subject and before the verb: Subject + Time + Verb. Pattern: 我+七点+起床。 Sentences: 我六点半起床 wǒ liù diǎn bàn qǐchuáng (I get up at 6:30), 我七点吃早饭 wǒ qī diǎn chī zǎofàn (I eat breakfast at seven), 我八点去学校 wǒ bā diǎn qù xuéxiào (I go to school at eight), 我十点睡觉 wǒ shí diǎn shuìjiào (I go to bed at ten). Songs and rhymes about the days of the week and real-life daily routines are used for memorisation. Learners write in characters with pinyin and read the sentences aloud.
sla_notes_illustrations: Daily routine. The learner writes: 我早上六点起床,七点吃早饭,八点上课,下午四点回家。Wǒ zǎoshang liù diǎn qǐchuáng, qī diǎn chī zǎofàn, bā diǎn shàng kè, xiàwǔ sì diǎn huí jiā.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing the time is useful for timetables, invitations and messages about when to meet.
sla_exercise: Write 'I go to school at eight' in Chinese.::我八点去学校。Wǒ bā diǎn qù xuéxiào.||Where does the time word go in a sentence?::After the subject and before the verb.||What does 我十点睡觉 mean?::I go to bed at ten o'clock.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to listen and understand information
learning_activity_name: Listen to a presentation and answer questions based on it
sla_name: Listening to a presentation and answering questions
sla_method: Note taking and Listen and retell
sla_assessment_criteria: Presentation are listened and questions based on presentation are answered.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to a short talk in Chinese and answer questions about it.
sla_notes_details: Note-taking helps recall: while listening, write key words such as names, numbers and places. After listening, answer questions, first orally and then in writing. Question words: 谁 shéi, 什么 shénme, 哪儿 nǎr, 什么时候 shénme shíhou, 为什么 wèi shénme, 几 jǐ. Learners then retell the main content in their own words. The presentation should be based on familiar topics such as 我的家 wǒ de jiā (my family) or 我的一天 wǒ de yì tiān (my day).
sla_notes_illustrations: Presentation: 我叫玛丽。我家有四口人。我爸爸是老师,妈妈是医生。Wǒ jiào Mǎlì. Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén. Wǒ bàba shì lǎoshī, māma shì yīshēng. Q: 玛丽的妈妈做什么工作? A: 她是医生。
sla_notes_daily_life: Listening with understanding is necessary for following talks, lectures, radio and video messages in Chinese.
sla_exercise: What does 医生 mean?::Doctor.||Which question word means 'why'?::为什么 (wèi shénme).||Why do learners take notes while listening?::To remember key details such as names, numbers and places so they can answer questions.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to listen and understand information
learning_activity_name: Listen to complex sentences and construct simple sentences using new words derived from them
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex sentences are listened and simple sentences using new words are constructed.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to complex sentences and pick out new words to build their own simple sentences.
sla_notes_details: Identify key information in the heard sentence, write the new words with pinyin, and then create a new short sentence with each word. Complex sentences contain link words such as 因为...所以... (because ... so ...), 但是, 如果...就... (if ... then ...). Example: 因为今天下雨,所以我在家学习。Yīnwèi jīntiān xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ zài jiā xuéxí. New words: 下雨 xià yǔ (to rain), 今天 jīntiān (today). Simple sentence: 今天下雨。Jīntiān xià yǔ.
sla_notes_illustrations: The learner hears 我的姐姐喜欢在厨房做蛋糕。Wǒ de jiějie xǐhuan zài chúfáng zuò dàngāo. New words: 喜欢 xǐhuan (like), 蛋糕 dàngāo (cake). New sentences: 我喜欢蛋糕。Wǒ xǐhuan dàngāo.
sla_notes_daily_life: Picking out and re-using new words is how learners build vocabulary from conversations, videos and songs.
sla_exercise: Translate 因为...所以...::Because ... therefore/so ...||What does 今天 mean?::Today.||Make a simple sentence using 蛋糕.::For example 我喜欢蛋糕 (I like cake).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to listen and understand information
learning_activity_name: Listen and reproduce complex sentences
sla_name: Listening to and repeating complex sentences
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex sentences are listened and reproduced.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to longer sentences, remember them and repeat them accurately.
sla_notes_details: Techniques: vocabulary building before listening; listening for meaning first and then for details; chunking sentences into meaningful groups; and repeating with the same rhythm. Complex sentences contain more than one clause, time words and link words. Example: 我每天早上七点起床,然后吃早饭,再去学校。Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng, ránhòu chī zǎofàn, zài qù xuéxiào. Learners repeat, first with support (key words on the board) and then without.
sla_notes_illustrations: Chunking: 我每天/早上七点/起床,/然后/吃早饭,/再去学校。 The learner repeats the chunks in order and then the whole sentence, and the teacher checks tone and word order.
sla_notes_daily_life: Being able to hold a longer sentence in memory helps learners take messages, follow directions and interpret.
sla_exercise: What does 每天 mean?::Every day.||Which word means 'then' in the example sentence?::然后 (ránhòu).||Why is a long sentence divided into chunks for repetition?::It is easier to remember and repeat correctly in meaningful groups.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to read and understand various texts
learning_activity_name: Identify new words used in a simple written text
sla_name: Identifying new words in a simple text
sla_method: Reading comprehension exercises and Contextual learning
sla_assessment_criteria: New words used in a simple written text are identified.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read a short text and find the words they do not yet know, using context and the dictionary.
sla_notes_details: Strategies: read the text once for meaning; underline unknown words; guess from context and radicals; check in a pinyin dictionary; record in a vocabulary book with pinyin, meaning and an example sentence. Radicals hint at meaning: 氵 relates to water (河 hé river, 湖 hú lake), 讠to speech (说 shuō speak, 请 qǐng invite), 口 to the mouth (吃 chī eat, 喝 hē drink), 木 to wood or trees (树 shù tree, 桌 zhuō table). Reading comprehension exercises follow.
sla_notes_illustrations: Text: 我家有一个大花园。花园里有很多树。Wǒ jiā yǒu yí gè dà huāyuán. Huāyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō shù. Unknown words: 花园 huāyuán (garden), 树 shù (tree). The radical 木 in 树 gives a clue that it means a tree.
sla_notes_daily_life: Working out new words from context helps learners read signs, articles and messages without stopping for a dictionary.
sla_exercise: What does the radical 氵 usually indicate?::Water.||What is 花园 in English?::Garden.||Name two things learners record for each new word in their vocabulary book.::The pinyin and the meaning (and an example sentence).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to read and understand various texts
learning_activity_name: Sequence the events in a story in a logical order
sla_method: Pre - reading Strategies and Active reading
sla_assessment_criteria: The events in a story are sequenced in a logical order.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read a short story and put the events in the correct order, using sequence words.
sla_notes_details: Sequence words: 首先 shǒuxiān (first), 然后 ránhòu (then), 接着 jiēzhe (next), 最后 zuìhòu (finally), 后来 hòulái (later). Reading strategies: preview the title and pictures, read for the main idea, note who did what and when, then number the events. Learners rearrange strips of sentences and retell the story orally in order. Active reading includes asking questions about the story as they read.
sla_notes_illustrations: Story strips: (a) 最后,他回到家。(b) 早上,小明去市场。(c) 然后,他买了香蕉。 Correct order: b, c, a. Retell: 首先小明去市场,然后他买了香蕉,最后他回到家。
sla_notes_daily_life: Ordering events helps learners narrate what happened, understand instructions with steps and write reports.
sla_exercise: How do you say 'finally' in Chinese?::最后 (zuìhòu).||Put in order: 然后 / 首先 / 最后.::首先, 然后, 最后 (first, then, finally).||What does 回到家 mean?::Return home.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Show the right response in various communicative contexts
learning_activity_name: Listen and respond to complex orders given in a home setting
sla_name: Responding to complex spoken orders at home
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex orders given in a home setting are listened to and responded to.
sla_teaching_aids: Downloaded video from YouTube with related contents
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to several-step orders given in a home setting and act on them correctly.
sla_notes_details: Home orders use verbs such as 洗 xǐ (wash), 打扫 dǎsǎo (sweep, clean), 做饭 zuò fàn (cook), 关 guān (close), 开 kāi (open), 拿 ná (take) and 放 fàng (put). The 把 bǎ pattern moves the object before the verb: 请把门关上 qǐng bǎ mén guānshàng (please close the door). Sequence words 先 and 再 link steps. Vocabulary is built before listening, and practice exercises use realistic tasks (for example laying the table).
sla_notes_illustrations: Order: 请先把桌子擦干净,然后把碗放在桌子上。Qǐng xiān bǎ zhuōzi cā gānjìng, ránhòu bǎ wǎn fàng zài zhuōzi shàng. The learner wipes the table and then puts the bowls on it.
sla_notes_daily_life: Following spoken orders is needed to help at home, cooperate at work and respond in Chinese-speaking families or workplaces.
sla_exercise: What does 关门 mean?::Close the door.||Translate 请把书放在桌子上。::Please put the book on the desk.||What is the function of 把 in a sentence?::It moves the object in front of the verb to show what is done to it.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Show the right response in various communicative contexts
learning_activity_name: Read and respond to complex orders given in a home setting
sla_name: Reading and responding to written orders at home
sla_assessment_criteria: Complex orders given in a home setting are read and responded.
sla_teaching_aids: Downloaded video from YouTube with related contents
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read a written order in a home setting and respond by carrying out the task or answering in writing.
sla_notes_details: Written orders may be notes on a fridge, a shopping list, or a recipe. Steps: read the order, underline the verbs and the objects, check unknown characters, do the task. Sample vocabulary: 买 mǎi (buy), 洗 xǐ (wash), 做 zuò (do, make), 带 dài (bring), 别 bié (do not), 不要 búyào (do not). Prohibitions use 不要 or 别: 别忘了关灯 bié wàng le guān dēng (do not forget to turn off the light). Learners do a project by writing their own set of home instructions and exchange them.
sla_notes_illustrations: Note on the door: 妈妈,我去市场了,请把饭放在冰箱里。Māma, wǒ qù shìchǎng le, qǐng bǎ fàn fàng zài bīngxiāng lǐ. Learner reads and puts the food in the fridge.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading household instructions is useful for following recipes, labels on appliances and messages from family.
sla_exercise: What does 别 mean in an order?::Do not.||Translate 请买两个苹果。::Please buy two apples.||How do you say 'turn off the light' in Chinese?::关灯 (guān dēng).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate understanding of information in conversation and writing
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to read correctly various texts
learning_activity_name: Read accurately simple sentences using standard speed, correct tone, pronunciation and punctuation marks
sla_method: Reading for comprehension exercises and Contextual learning
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences using standard speed, correct tone, pronunciation and punctuation marks are read accurately.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners read simple sentences aloud at a standard speed, with correct tones, pronunciation and punctuation.
sla_notes_details: Accuracy means: every syllable pronounced clearly, tones correct, tone changes applied, pauses at commas (short) and full stops (longer), and rising intonation for questions. Steps: read silently for meaning, mark the pauses, read aloud slowly, then at natural speed. Comprehension exercises after reading check understanding. Sentences include questions with 吗 and 呢, exclamations with 啊 and 吧, and lists with 、.
sla_notes_illustrations: Reading: 你今天几点回家? 我四点回家,你呢? Nǐ jīntiān jǐ diǎn huí jiā? Wǒ sì diǎn huí jiā, nǐ ne? The learner pauses at the comma, uses rising intonation for the questions and reads 不 as bú where needed.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading accurately builds confidence for presentations and for reading aloud in class and at school events.
sla_exercise: How does the voice change at the end of a yes/no question?::It rises slightly.||What is the function of 吗 at the end of a sentence?::It turns a statement into a yes/no question.||How long should the pause be at a comma compared with a full stop?::Shorter at a comma than at a full stop.

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in a variety of contexts
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to communicate orally
learning_activity_name: Pronounce different phrases in various contexts
sla_assessment_criteria: Different phrases in various contexts are pronounced.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners pronounce common phrases correctly in contexts such as greeting, shopping and asking for help.
sla_notes_details: Common phrases: 请问 qǐngwèn (excuse me, may I ask), 对不起 duìbuqǐ (sorry), 没关系 méi guānxi (it does not matter), 麻烦你 máfan nǐ (sorry to trouble you), 请再说一遍 qǐng zài shuō yí biàn (please say it again), 我不明白 wǒ bù míngbai (I do not understand), 你说得太快了 nǐ shuō de tài kuài le (you speak too fast). Phrases are pronounced as one unit with natural rhythm. Reflective listening: after a partner speaks, the listener repeats the sentence to confirm the meaning and pronunciation.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role play at a bus stop. A: 请问,去市场怎么走? Qǐngwèn, qù shìchǎng zěnme zǒu? B: 一直走,然后往左拐。Yìzhí zǒu, ránhòu wǎng zuǒ guǎi. A: 谢谢! B: 不客气。
sla_notes_daily_life: Common phrases let learners ask for help, get directions and be polite when speaking to Chinese speakers.
sla_exercise: Translate 请再说一遍。::Please say it again.||What does 我不明白 mean?::I do not understand.||Which phrase is used to say 'excuse me, may I ask'?::请问 (qǐngwèn).

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in a variety of contexts
specific_competence_name: Develop the ability to communicate orally
learning_activity_name: Participate in a simple conversation (e.g. asking for permission)
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple conversation (e.g. asking for permission) are participated in.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners take part in short dialogues where they ask for permission and give or refuse it politely.
sla_notes_details: Asking: 我可以...吗? wǒ kěyǐ ... ma? (may I ...?) Giving: 可以 kěyǐ (yes, you may). Refusing: 不可以 bù kěyǐ or 对不起,现在不行 duìbuqǐ, xiànzài bù xíng (sorry, not now). Examples: 老师,我可以进来吗? lǎoshī, wǒ kěyǐ jìnlái ma? (teacher, may I come in?), 我可以用你的笔吗? wǒ kěyǐ yòng nǐ de bǐ ma? (may I use your pen?). Learners note the polite word 请 for granting: 请进 qǐng jìn (please come in). Note taking and role play are used to prepare dialogues.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue. A: 老师,我可以去厕所吗? Lǎoshī, wǒ kěyǐ qù cèsuǒ ma? B: 可以,去吧。Kěyǐ, qù ba. A: 谢谢老师。Xièxie lǎoshī.
sla_notes_daily_life: Asking for permission politely is important at school, at work and in someone else's home.
sla_exercise: How do you say 'May I come in?' in Chinese?::我可以进来吗? (wǒ kěyǐ jìnlái ma?)||What does 不可以 mean?::You may not (not allowed).||Give a polite reply that grants permission.::可以,请进。 (Yes, please come in.)

main_competence_name: Communicate effectively in a variety of contexts
specific_competence_name: Developing the ability to communicate accurately in writing in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Communicate in chat groups using social media such as WeChat, Telegram and WhatsApp by using short messages
sla_name: Communicating by short messages on social media
sla_assessment_criteria: Short messages are used to communicate in chat groups on social media such as WeChat, Telegram and WhatsApp.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write short messages in Chinese chat groups such as WeChat, Telegram and WhatsApp, using correct and polite language.
sla_notes_details: Chat messages are short and informal, but should still be clear. Useful messages: 你好! nǐ hǎo! 在吗? zài ma? (are you there?), 好的 hǎo de (OK), 没问题 méi wèntí (no problem), 谢谢 xièxie, 明天见 míngtiān jiàn (see you tomorrow), 晚安 wǎn'ān (good night), 生日快乐 shēngrì kuàilè (happy birthday). Learners type with a pinyin keyboard: type the pinyin and choose the character. Good practice: use polite forms, do not use offensive words, keep messages short, and avoid sharing private information. Learners create a class chat group and discuss topics in it.
sla_notes_illustrations: Class chat. A: 大家好!明天几点上课? Dàjiā hǎo! Míngtiān jǐ diǎn shàng kè? B: 八点。Bā diǎn. A: 好的,谢谢! Hǎo de, xièxie!
sla_notes_daily_life: Using Chinese on social media allows learners to keep in touch with friends and practise the language every day.
sla_exercise: What does 在吗? mean in chat?::Are you there?||How do you type Chinese characters with a pinyin keyboard?::Type the pinyin and select the correct character from the list.||Write 'Happy birthday' in Chinese.::生日快乐 (shēngrì kuàilè).

specific_competence_name: Develop awareness of Chinese phonemes, initial, final, tone and characters
learning_activity_name: Listen to Chinese words in pinyin while observing appropriate sequencing of tones
sla_name: Listening to pinyin and tone sequences
sla_assessment_criteria: Chinese words in pinyin are listened while observing appropriate sequencing of tones.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to Chinese words in pinyin and notice how tones combine and change when several syllables are joined.
sla_notes_details: In two-syllable words there are twenty possible tone combinations, and each has a pattern. Learners listen for the order of the tones and mark them: tone 1 + tone 1 (Zhōngguó has 1+2), 3 + 3 changes to 2 + 3 (nǐ hǎo → ní hǎo), 4 + 4 falls twice (zàijiàn 再见, tòngkuài). In three third tones the first two change to second tone if the words are read as one group: 我很好 wǒ hěn hǎo → wó hén hǎo. 不 and 一 change according to the tone that follows (bú shì, yí gè, yì tiān). Mnemonic aids and tone-chart games help retention.
sla_notes_illustrations: Listening task. The teacher reads shǒubiǎo 手表 (watch), yǔsǎn 雨伞 (umbrella), and hǎo jiǔ 好久 (a long time). Learners write the tone numbers 3-3, 3-3, 3-3 and then note the change to 2-3 in each.
sla_notes_daily_life: Recognising tone combinations helps learners follow fast speech in songs, news and conversations.
sla_exercise: Which tone change happens when two third tones are together?::The first third tone changes to a second tone.||How is 不是 pronounced?::bú shì.||How is 一天 pronounced?::yì tiān.

specific_competence_name: Develop awareness of Chinese phonemes, initial, final, tone and characters
learning_activity_name: Participate in a conversation while observing appropriate sequencing of tones
sla_name: Taking part in conversation with correct tone sequences
sla_assessment_criteria: Sequencing of tones are observed appropriately while participating in Conversation.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners join in conversations while applying tone changes and neutral tones correctly.
sla_notes_details: Prepared dialogues include tone changes. Learners mark each change before role playing: for example 你好 (ní hǎo), 不好 (bù hǎo), 一起 (yì qǐ), 很好 (hěn hǎo), 不要 (bú yào). The neutral tone appears in particles (吗 ma, 呢 ne, 吧 ba, 的 de, 了 le) and the second syllable of doubled words (妈妈 māma, 看看 kànkan). Partners record their dialogue, listen back and correct tones. Mnemonic and role-play methods are used.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue. A: 你好吗? Nǐ hǎo ma? B: 很好,你呢? Hěn hǎo, nǐ ne? A: 我也很好。我们一起去学校吧? Wǒmen yìqǐ qù xuéxiào ba? B: 好啊。Hǎo a.
sla_notes_daily_life: Applying tone changes helps speech sound natural in real conversations with Chinese friends and colleagues.
sla_exercise: Which particle marks a suggestion, as in 我们走吧?::吧 (ba).||How is 一起 pronounced?::yìqǐ (yī becomes yì before a third tone).||What does 你呢? mean?::And you?

specific_competence_name: Develop awareness of Chinese phonemes, initial, final, tone and characters
learning_activity_name: Write Chinese characters with 14-15 strokes
sla_name: Writing Chinese characters of 14 to 15 strokes
sla_assessment_criteria: Chinese characters with 14-15 strokes are written.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write characters that have fourteen and fifteen strokes with correct stroke order and structure.
sla_notes_details: Characters with 14 strokes include 静 jìng (quiet), 算 suàn (calculate), 精 jīng (refined), 漂 piào (as in 漂亮 piàoliang, beautiful). Characters with 15 strokes include 影 yǐng (shadow, as in 电影 diànyǐng, film), 德 dé (virtue), 题 tí (topic, question), 熟 shú (familiar). Complex characters are written by component: left before right, top before bottom. Learners write in a big grid first, then in the normal size, and check by counting strokes. Games and activities such as stroke-order relays and character puzzles consolidate learning.
sla_notes_illustrations: Writing 题 tí (question, topic): left part 是 (9 strokes) then right part 页 (6 strokes), total 15. Learners count and copy it three times, then use it in 问题 wèntí (problem, question).
sla_notes_daily_life: Complex characters appear in film titles, newspaper headings and exam questions, so accurate writing supports reading and typing.
sla_exercise: How many strokes does 静 have?::Fourteen strokes.||What does 电影 mean?::Film (movie).||Write the pinyin for 题.::tí.

specific_competence_name: Master the correct Chinese vocabulary in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Write new words associated with the market environment
sla_assessment_criteria: New words associated with the market environment are written.
sla_teaching_aids: Written text|Pictures that display the market
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write words about shopping and the market: goods, prices and people.
sla_notes_details: Vocabulary: 市场 shìchǎng (market), 商店 shāngdiàn (shop), 买 mǎi (buy), 卖 mài (sell), 钱 qián (money), 价格 jiàgé (price), 便宜 piányi (cheap), 贵 guì (expensive), 苹果 píngguǒ (apple), 香蕉 xiāngjiāo (banana), 西红柿 xīhóngshì (tomato), 鱼 yú (fish), 肉 ròu (meat), 蔬菜 shūcài (vegetables), 米 mǐ (rice), 面包 miànbāo (bread). Money: 元 yuán, 块 kuài, 分 fēn; in Tanzania 先令 xiānlìng (shilling). Numbers above ten: 十 shí, 二十 èrshí, 一百 yì bǎi, 一千 yì qiān. Measure words: 斤 jīn (half kilogram), 个 gè, 公斤 gōngjīn. Learners use written labels and price tags in a mock market.
sla_notes_illustrations: Mock market. Learners write price tags: 苹果 五百先令 (píngguǒ wǔbǎi xiānlìng), 鱼 三千先令 (yú sānqiān xiānlìng), 米 两千先令 (mǐ liǎngqiān xiānlìng), and label each stall with its goods.
sla_notes_daily_life: Market vocabulary is useful when shopping, trading with Chinese customers and reading labels on Chinese products.
sla_exercise: What is 便宜 in English?::Cheap.||How do you write 'market' in Chinese and pinyin?::市场, shìchǎng.||Write 'one hundred' in Chinese.::一百 (yì bǎi).

specific_competence_name: Master the correct Chinese vocabulary in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Construct simple oral sentences using new words associated with the market environment
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple oral sentences using new words associated with the market environment are constructed.
sla_teaching_aids: Written text|Pictures that display the market
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners create spoken sentences with market vocabulary, asking prices and quantities and bargaining politely.
sla_notes_details: Key sentences: 你要什么? nǐ yào shénme? (what do you want?), 我要买...wǒ yào mǎi ... (I want to buy ...), 多少钱? duōshao qián? (how much?), 一斤多少钱? yì jīn duōshao qián? (how much per jin?), 太贵了 tài guì le (too expensive), 便宜一点儿 piányi yìdiǎnr (a bit cheaper), 可以 kěyǐ (OK), 给你钱 gěi nǐ qián (here is the money). Verb+object combinations and measure words are stressed: 三个苹果 sān gè píngguǒ (three apples), 两斤鱼 liǎng jīn yú (two jin of fish). Dictogloss is used: the teacher reads a text twice and learners reconstruct it from notes.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role play. Buyer: 这个苹果多少钱? Zhège píngguǒ duōshao qián? Seller: 一个五百先令。Yí gè wǔbǎi xiānlìng. Buyer: 太贵了,便宜一点儿吧。Tài guì le, piányi yìdiǎnr ba. Seller: 好,四百先令。Hǎo, sìbǎi xiānlìng.
sla_notes_daily_life: Being able to ask prices and bargain helps learners in shops, tourism work and trade with Chinese-speaking customers.
sla_exercise: How do you ask 'How much is it?'::多少钱? (duōshao qián?)||Say 'Too expensive' in Chinese.::太贵了 (tài guì le).||Translate 我要买三个苹果。::I want to buy three apples.

specific_competence_name: Master the correct Chinese vocabulary in various contexts
learning_activity_name: Write simple sentences using new words associated with the market environment
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences using new words associated with the market environment are written.
sla_teaching_aids: Written text|Pictures that display the market
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners write sentences about shopping and the market, using vocabulary, measure words and punctuation.
sla_notes_details: Written sentences use the pattern Subject + Verb + Number + Measure word + Noun. Examples: 我在市场买了三个苹果 wǒ zài shìchǎng mǎi le sān gè píngguǒ (I bought three apples at the market), 妈妈买了两斤鱼 māma mǎi le liǎng jīn yú (mother bought two jin of fish). The particle 了 marks a completed action. Learners write the total price, e.g. 一共一千五百先令 yígòng yìqiān wǔbǎi xiānlìng (in total 1,500 shillings). Dictogloss and writing prompts are used to plan and check the sentences.
sla_notes_illustrations: Shopping list. 我要买:苹果三个,香蕉五个,西红柿两斤。Wǒ yào mǎi: píngguǒ sān gè, xiāngjiāo wǔ gè, xīhóngshì liǎng jīn. Learner writes total price sentence: 一共两千先令。
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing shopping lists and receipts in Chinese is useful for trade and for communicating with Chinese-speaking customers.
sla_exercise: Write in Chinese: I want to buy two kilograms of rice.::我要买两公斤米。Wǒ yào mǎi liǎng gōngjīn mǐ.||What does 一共 mean?::In total.||What does the particle 了 show in 我买了苹果?::That the action of buying has been completed.

specific_competence_name: Develop the use of appropriate grammar and vocabulary in conversation and writing
learning_activity_name: Listen and respond to simple sentences
sla_name: Listening and responding to simple sentences
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences listened and responded.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners listen to simple sentences in different situations and respond suitably.
sla_notes_details: Listening practice uses recorded dialogues and teacher speech. Response types: answering a question (你叫什么名字?), agreeing or disagreeing (对,不对), giving information (我是学生), and doing an action. Dialogue technique: teacher asks, learner answers in a full sentence, then learners swap roles. Common question-answer pairs: 你是哪国人? Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén? — 我是坦桑尼亚人。 你几岁? Nǐ jǐ suì? — 我十五岁。 你住在哪儿? Nǐ zhù zài nǎr? — 我住在达累斯萨拉姆。
sla_notes_illustrations: Audio: 你是哪国人? Learners write the answer 我是坦桑尼亚人。Wǒ shì Tǎnsāngníyà rén. The teacher plays the next question, 你几岁? and the learner answers with their own age.
sla_notes_daily_life: Answering simple questions quickly is essential in everyday conversations, interviews and customer service.
sla_exercise: Answer in Chinese: 你是哪国人?::我是坦桑尼亚人 (wǒ shì Tǎnsāngníyà rén).||What does 你几岁? ask?::How old are you?||Translate 我住在达累斯萨拉姆。::I live in Dar es Salaam.

specific_competence_name: Develop the use of appropriate grammar and vocabulary in conversation and writing
learning_activity_name: Use different words to construct simple oral sentences
sla_name: Constructing oral sentences with different words
sla_assessment_criteria: Different words are used to construct oral simple sentences.
sla_references: TET(2023), CHINESE LANGUAGE SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners use a range of new words to make simple spoken sentences.
sla_notes_details: Learners study the parts of speech: nouns (书), verbs (读), adjectives (大, 好), adverbs (很, 也, 都), measure words (个, 本) and particles (的, 了, 吗). Building blocks: Subject + Adverb + Verb + Object (我也喜欢音乐 wǒ yě xǐhuan yīnyuè, I also like music), Subject + 很 + Adjective (天气很好 tiānqì hěn hǎo), possession with 的 (我的书 wǒ de shū). Dialogue-based activities and game-like tasks such as 'add one word' encourage varied sentences.
sla_notes_illustrations: Add-one-word game. Start: 我喜欢书。 → 我喜欢汉语书。 → 我也喜欢汉语书。 → 我和朋友都喜欢汉语书。Each learner extends the sentence with one word, saying it aloud.
sla_notes_daily_life: Building sentences from many words gives learners flexibility to talk about their interests and daily life.
sla_exercise: Translate 我也喜欢音乐。::I also like music.||What is the function of 的 in 我的书?::It shows possession (my book).||Which word means 'all' or 'both' in 我们都是学生?::都 (dōu).

specific_competence_name: Develop the use of appropriate grammar and vocabulary in conversation and writing
learning_activity_name: Write simple sentences using different words
sla_name: Writing simple sentences with different words
sla_assessment_criteria: Simple sentences are written using simple words.
